strings.name: Roger Myerson
strings.role: Economist · University of Chicago professor emeritus
strings.summary: Myerson uses game theory and mechanism design to study information, incentives and institutions. His work spans auctions, bilateral trade and political systems. He shared the 2007 economics Nobel with Hurwicz and Maskin. After long appointments at Northwestern and Chicago, he retired in 2026 and delivered a valedictory lecture.

strings.influence.rationale: Studies game theory and mechanism design, applying information and incentives to economic and political institutions.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Harvard applied-mathematics AB and SM (1973), PhD (1976).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Information and incentives
strings.highlights.h1.text: Uses incentive constraints to connect private information with attainable social outcomes.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Economic and political institutions
strings.highlights.h2.text: Applies game theory to auctions, trade, elections and local governance.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Valedictory lecture marking retirement
strings.timeline.t1.text: Spoke at Harris on 7 October about local politics and institutions; the university subsequently reported the celebration.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Shared economics Nobel
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won with Leonid Hurwicz and Eric Maskin for foundations of mechanism design.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joined Chicago
strings.timeline.t3.text: Moved after 25 years at Northwestern to continue his research.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Game-theory book published
strings.timeline.t4.text: Game Theory: Analysis of Conflict systematically explained strategic interaction and information.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Bilateral-trade paper
strings.timeline.t5.text: With Mark Satterthwaite, analyzed efficiency limits under private information.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Optimal-auction paper
strings.timeline.t6.text: Characterized seller-revenue maximization subject to incentive constraints.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Refined Nash equilibrium
strings.timeline.t7.text: Developed refinement criteria for selecting strategically stable outcomes.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Doctorate and Northwestern appointment
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed Harvard’s applied-mathematics doctorate and began teaching managerial economics and decision sciences.
